caption:
Valentina Vaulet was named to the All-Big Ten First team, wrapping an incredible season at University of Oregon @oregonvb 🌟🦆

Vaulet became just the sixth Duck in only two seasons of Big Ten play to earn all-conference honors, and the fourth ever to make the First Team.

Vaulet finished the regular season inside the top 15 of the Big Ten with a career-high 371 kills, good for 3.20 kills per set. She also posted career highs with a .266 hitting percentage and 454.5 points.

The junior from Argentina reached double-digit kills in 23 of 30 games and during the opening weekend of Big Ten play, Vaulet recorded a career-high 2️⃣8️⃣ kills. She also finished the season with three double-doubles and leads the conference with 56 aces. Vaulet had at least one ace in 27 of 30 matches including a career-high tying six aces at Maryland.

A great year and one of the best we’ve seen in a Duck uniform. We are so proud of you Val, all your determination and hard work are paying off! 💚💛 #GoDucks

caption:
6 years. 4 schools. 3 states. And more memories than I could ever count.
From starting my career in 2020 at the University of Montana, to playing at Portland State on the other side of the net at Matthew Knight, to winning a WCC Championship at LMU and to finishing my college career in the Big Ten at Oregon. This journey has been anything but easy, but it has been everything I could have ever dreamed of. 
These years have been a roller coaster of the highest highs, the lowest lows, the friendships that felt like family, the heartbreak losses, the travel, the growth, the doubt, the breakthroughs. Most importantly, they’ve been a journey back to myself.
After my first year of college, I made a promise to never settle, put myself first, and show up every single day to become better. That promise has guided me through every single day.  It pushed me to trust the unknown, to take risks even when I was so scared, and to believe that I deserved more than comfort — I deserved growth and belief. 
Looking back now, I wouldn’t change a single part of this path. 
Every twist, every challenge, every person who entered or exited my life shaped me into the athlete and woman I am today. I’m grateful for the people who believed in me, the ones who doubted me, the ones who stood by me, and the ones who left. Each one played a role in my strength and determination. 
If there’s one thing this journey taught me, you are capable of rewriting your story at any moment. You’re allowed to outgrow places, people, and versions of yourself. You’re allowed to chase something bigger, even when it scares you.
Im ending my college career proud — not just of what I accomplished, but of who I became along the way. Stay tuned for what’s next… 💚✨

You had the softest voice that could always put me at ease. You were and always will be the love of my life. I love you my sweet Gramps. Say hello to everyone for me. caption:
Thank you Wilsonville and this team for an amazing senior season🤍🤞🏼

With some unwritten future ahead it’s hard to believe this chapter is potentially coming to a close for me. I truly believe there is not one thing in my life I have worked so hard for or spent so much dedicated time on like I have baseball. It has been the highest of highs and at times the lowest of lows. If baseball has taught me one thing it is how to work. I’ve learned over and over again that baseball truly owes you nothing, the question  becomes, how much are you willing to sacrifice to be the best version of yourself? When you love something you give it your all. Inspite of failure inspite of unwanted results you keep going. If you’re a competitor failure sucks, you reject failure. Baseball has taught me how to move forward even in what at times seems like failure. I am forever grateful for every opportunity, moment, and  life changing experience I’ve been so fortunate to have in this sport. Thank you to everyone who has made this journey so influential and no one more important than my dad. Forever in debt to you for all the trips, lessons and memories along the way. Love you big man🫶🏼

🏅 2x State Volleyball Champion
🏅 2023 Conference Player of the Year
🏅 2x 1st Team All-Conference and 1st Team All-State

Kamden will be attending the University of Oregon to play both Indoor and Beach Volleyball while pursuing a degree in Business Administration with a focus on Marketing, Law, or Human Resources.

athlete.name: Brady Bidwell
athlete.bio: A relentless competitor, this wide receiver combines agility and sharp route-running with a keen football IQ. Hailing from a small town, his tenacity and team spirit inspire both teammates and fans alike.

caption:
Marist Football has created the greatest senior season of football I could have asked for. Looking back to last summer and my whole season up in the air with transferring to a new school, it’s such a blessing to see how God introduced me to these amazing brothers. As emotional as an ending can be, my high school football career has given me the best memories and experiences of my life. It’s given me the strongest relationships and taught me the most important lessons. Being able to, all my life, play this sport with my brother and my dad on the side as the coach since my first season is one of the greatest gifts the Lord has given me. Thank you Marist for one of the happiest times of my life and greatest memories, and I can’t wait to open a new chapter as I continue with this sport I love. 

@shotbygaryy @midmajormedia @maristcatholicfootball @maristcatholicathletics @maristspartans

Wow — what a day.
 
I’ve played football almost my whole life. Reaching this moment is something I am incredibly thankful for. 
 
I’d like to thank my Lord and Savior Jesus Christ; without you, nothing is possible.
 
Thank you to my family. Friends. Coaches. Trainers. Mentors. All who have made a difference in this journey. You know who you are — I wouldn’t have made it without you.
